finding: The live range of $480-$2,450 is too low at the bottom; its top is about right for federal-emissions and OEM parts but too low where a California-emissions (CARB) part is required. Built totals per converter (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $1,067-$2,077 (0.9-1.4 hr); midsize 2016 Camry about $778-$1,608 (1.3-1.6 hr); truck 2016 F-150 5.0L about $824-$1,697 (0.9-2.3 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $553-$1,839 (1.3-1.8 hr). With the CARB-compliant aftermarket part instead: Corolla about $2,017-$2,133, Camry about $1,328-$1,428, F-150 about $2,576-$2,836; no CARB aftermarket part was found for the BMW. So the lowest total we can build is about $553, and that needs the cheapest federal-only part at a sale price ($397); mainstream cars start near $780-$1,070. $480 is below anything found. Labor is the small part of this job (0.9-2.3 hours, about $110-$370); the converter itself decides the price. At the top, federal and OEM builds reach about $2,080, inside $2,450, but a CARB part on the truck comes to about $2,580-$2,840 and benchmarks run higher still (RepairPal average $2,293-$2,468, AAA $1,000-$4,000, ConsumerAffairs samples $933-$4,414). Roughly $550-$2,100 for federal-emissions vehicles and up to about $2,850 or more in CARB states fits the evidence. How solid the labor times are: only the truck time is for the example model (Ford's times for the 2022-2023 F-150 5.0L, not the 2016 model year). The economy times are a Honda warranty time for a CR-Z (0.9 hr) and a Kia recall time for a Soul (1.4 hr, including a software update), not Toyota times for the Corolla; a Toyota bulletin for the same kind of front-pipe converter on a Tacoma gives 0.7. The midsize times are a GM warranty time for a front-wheel-drive Equinox (1.3 hr; 2.6 hr with all-wheel drive) and a Honda time for a 2010 Accord V6 that also covers a sensor and diagnosis (1.6 hr), not Camry times. The luxury times are Acura warranty times for a turbo four-cylinder RDX (1.3-1.8 hr), not BMW times. These are manufacturer times on clean, newer vehicles; rusted or seized exhaust hardware takes longer. Other caveats: several retailer pages did not state converter position; the Corolla has only one priced federal aftermarket listing; the Camry's OEM manifold converter ($490 list) is cheaper than the front-pipe converter used for the high figure.
extras: Quotes often add oxygen or air-fuel sensors (frequently replaced or seized during removal), new gaskets, studs, nuts and clamps, a diagnosis fee for the catalyst-efficiency code, shop supplies and sales tax. Vehicles with two or more converters may need more than one. In California and other CARB states only CARB-compliant or OEM converters are legal, which can double the parts price; federal-only parts cannot be installed there. A converter usually fails for a reason (misfire, oil or coolant burning), so repairs to the root cause may be quoted too. A failed original converter may still be covered by the federal emissions warranty (8 years / 80,000 miles), and theft replacement may be an insurance claim.
